title: [soundness] zero-initialized pointer declarations accepted; first use SIGSEGVs at runtime (memory safety)
body:
### The smallest .hy program that demonstrates it

```hy
package main

struct bag {
    counts map[string]int
}

fn main() {
    var p *bag
    fmt.println(p == nil)
    p.counts["k"] = 1
    fmt.println(len(p.counts))
}
```
Command: `hyb check ptr.hy` — `hyb` (MVP-0), built from main @ b1627e8 (2026-11-18).

### What the checker should say

Reject with a use-before-assignment diagnostic (e.g. HYB-E3199): `p` is a zero-initialized pointer declaration (`var p *bag`), so it holds nil; `p.counts["k"] = 1` writes through nil and `len(p.counts)` reads through nil — both SIGSEGV at runtime. Per GUARANTEES.md an accepted program must be memory-safe; this one crashes on first run.

### What it actually said

```
OK (0 diagnostics)
```

### Anything else

Comparison-only use (`p == nil`) is legal and should stay legal — which is why a blanket reject of `var p *T` would be wrong. A deref-gated use-before-assignment check (flag only dereferences: map-index write bases, field/index reads/writes through the binding) catches both crashes here while leaving `p == nil`, plain copies, and the `p != nil`-guarded idiom untouched. Full corpus diff vs main (141 files in tests/checker-corpus) shows 0 verdict changes with that gate. Work + 2-commit fix pushed at https://github.com/wminno/Go-Hybrid/tree/e3199-deref-v2 (commits b2bb4c9 + 0636bfb) — PR could not be opened with the available token.
